unit.title: Reliable Logistic Core: From Equation to Tested Python
unit.scope: Implement and independently verify a small, numerically stable binary logistic-loss core using the Python standard library.
prerequisite_assumptions: Comfort with algorithms and asymptotic analysis
learning_objectives: Turn mathematical assumptions into explicit software contracts.
Implement stable logit, sigmoid, binary-loss, and analytic-gradient calculations.
Design deterministic tests for normal, boundary, and invalid inputs.
Check analytic gradients against an independent finite-difference oracle.
Record reproducible execution evidence and analyze time and space cost.

unit_completion_requires: The test command completes successfully in the declared environment.
An independent examiner applies examiner_only/RUBRIC.md and awards at least 80 out of 100.
The mathematical-correctness, contract-safety, and verification rubric minima are each met.
completion_policy.completion_authority: A validator controlled by the worker harness or an explicitly assigned independent examiner; learner prose and self-reported logs are supporting evidence only.
completion_policy.course_completion_requires: A later, separately authorized expansion must identify, make available, schedule, and validate the remaining course units. The catalog estimate is 80 hours; this kickoff covers only 6 hours and cannot satisfy whole-course completion.
